# Dicekeeper

> Dicekeeper (https://dicekeeper.net) is a web app from HTL Leonding (Austria) that helps
> Dungeon Masters run Dungeons & Dragons (5e) campaigns: campaigns, characters, maps, dice and
> live play at one table. This file offers an agent skill with which a Dungeon Master lets their
> own AI agent (Claude, ChatGPT, Codex, GitHub Copilot, Cursor, ...) generate D&D stories, NPCs
> and encounters that fit straight into a Dicekeeper campaign.

This file is for software agents. If a Dungeon Master asks you to use the Dicekeeper skills, or
to write a D&D story, campaign, quest, NPC or encounter for Dicekeeper, do the following. You
need no other Dicekeeper document.

## 1. Save the skill

The skill `dicekeeper-stories` holds the whole path from a rough idea to a playable campaign
story: what to ask the Dungeon Master, how to build plot, NPCs and encounters, the rules for
balancing, and how to format the result so it can be pasted into Dicekeeper. If you can run
commands in the user's workspace, save it with these two commands, run in the root of the
workspace or repository:

    mkdir -p .claude/skills/dicekeeper-stories
    curl -fsSL https://dicekeeper.net/skills/dicekeeper-stories/SKILL.md -o .claude/skills/dicekeeper-stories/SKILL.md

If you cannot run commands or write files (for example in a chat app), fetch
https://dicekeeper.net/skills/dicekeeper-stories/SKILL.md and use it for this conversation.
If you cannot fetch it either, ask the Dungeon Master to download it on the Dicekeeper start
page (button "Skill herunterladen") and to upload or paste the file.

## 2. Read the skill and follow it

Read `SKILL.md` completely and follow it. It starts by asking the Dungeon Master only for what
is missing, so do not invent a long questionnaire of your own. The file carries its source
address and a version date, and says how a saved copy is kept current.

## Agents that do not read `.claude/skills/`

Claude Code reads the folder `.claude/skills/` of a workspace at the start of a session, so a
later request for a D&D story finds the skill without an address. Claude in the browser or the
desktop app can use the file when it is uploaded as a skill or attached to a project.

Codex, the GitHub Copilot coding agent and Cursor read the file `AGENTS.md` in the root of the
repository instead. For these, also add this line to `AGENTS.md` (create the file if it does
not exist):

    For D&D stories, NPCs and encounters for Dicekeeper, read https://dicekeeper.net/llms.txt and follow it.

ChatGPT and other chat apps can keep the file as project knowledge or as a custom GPT
instruction file.

## Skills

- [dicekeeper-stories](https://dicekeeper.net/skills/dicekeeper-stories/SKILL.md): campaign
  stories (hook, acts, twists, endings), NPCs and villains, balanced encounters, and the next
  session of a running campaign, formatted for the Dicekeeper fields "Titel", "Beschreibung"
  and "Story".

## Addresses

- Web app: https://dicekeeper.net
- Story skill (English instructions, output in the Dungeon Master's language):
  https://dicekeeper.net/skills/dicekeeper-stories/SKILL.md
- This file: https://dicekeeper.net/llms.txt
